title: AWS VPC Endpoint Requirements Matrix — Redwood Private (VPC) Terraform modules (alpha)
content:
Owner: Victor Alvarez (Infra)
Last updated: 2025-02-20
Scope: AWS PrivateLink / VPC endpoints used for Redwood Private (VPC) deployments. This matrix is used by:
- Terraform module defaults (`modules/vpc-endpoints` + wrapper `modules/redwood-private-vpc`)
- Installer networking preflight checks (reachability + DNS)
- Security review of “private-only egress” deployments

How to read this sheet
- “Required (Alpha)” means: if customer has restricted/zero public egress, we must provide an endpoint path for the dependency OR explicitly document that the topology is unsupported.
- “Depends” means: required only if the customer enables the referenced feature (e.g., SSM session manager, S3 log sink).
- Private DNS: “Yes (recommended)” means we should default to enabling Private DNS on the endpoint unless customer DNS architecture prevents it.
- Component labels:
  - Installer: `redwood-private-installer` (bootstrap + preflight)
  - Control plane: Redwood Private control plane services deployed in VPC
  - Data plane: inference/workload nodes (GPU nodes)
  - Observability: log/metrics forwarders, health checks

================================================================================
MATRIX (spreadsheet-style)
================================================================================
Columns:
Service | Endpoint name(s) | Type | Required (Alpha) | Private DNS | Why needed | Components that depend on it | Notes / endpoint policy guidance | Terraform support (alpha)

1) Container image pulls + artifacts
ECR (API) | com.amazonaws.${region}.ecr.api | Interface | Yes (if no public egress) | Yes (recommended) | Auth + image manifest/token operations for pulling Redwood images | Installer, Control plane, Data plane | Endpoint policy: restrict to required repos if customer mirrors; otherwise allow ecr:* for account/region; security prefers least privilege but avoid brittle repo ARNs during alpha | Supported (default on)
ECR (Docker) | com.amazonaws.${region}.ecr.dkr | Interface | Yes (if no public egress) | Yes (recommended) | Actual image layer pulls from ECR | Installer, Control plane, Data plane | Must be paired with S3 gateway endpoint for layer blob fetches; missing this is #1 pilot failure mode | Supported (default on)
S3 (Gateway) | com.amazonaws.${region}.s3 | Gateway | Yes (if no public egress) | N/A | ECR image layers and artifacts are backed by S3; also used for optional backups/log export | Installer, Control plane, Data plane, Observability | Route table association must include all subnets where nodes run; common misconfig = only private subnets associated, but “isolated” tier used by nodes | Supported (default on)

2) Identity / credentials
STS | com.amazonaws.${region}.sts | Interface | Yes (for assumed roles / temp creds; esp. locked-down) | Yes (recommended) | Instances/pods often use STS to assume roles (IRSA/instance profile flows vary) | Installer (preflight), Control plane, Data plane | Pilot issue: missing STS endpoint causes intermittent auth failures even when ECR/S3 are present; ensure DNS resolution works | Supported (default on in wrapper; can be toggled)
IAM | (no VPC endpoint) | N/A | No | N/A | IAM API has no standard VPC endpoint; access requires public egress OR performed outside VPC context | N/A | Guidance: perform IAM provisioning from admin workstation/CI with internet access; do not require runtime access | N/A

3) Logs / telemetry
CloudWatch Logs | com.amazonaws.${region}.logs | Interface | Depends (Yes if using CloudWatch Logs sink) | Yes (recommended) | Push application/system logs without NAT/internet | Control plane, Data plane, Observability | If customer uses an alternative sink (Splunk/Elastic/etc.), can disable; if enabled, validate log group + retention via IaC standards | Supported (default on in “standard” example)
CloudWatch Monitoring (Metrics) | com.amazonaws.${region}.monitoring | Interface | Depends | Yes (recommended) | Publish custom metrics to CloudWatch (if customer chooses CW metrics) | Observability, Control plane | Many customers don’t want CloudWatch metrics; ok to disable if using Prometheus/OTel to internal sink | Supported (optional)
X-Ray | com.amazonaws.${region}.xray | Interface | Optional | Yes (recommended) | Trace export for debugging | Observability | Not required for alpha; avoid enabling by default to reduce noise/cost | Not default; optional

4) Systems management / break-glass access
SSM | com.amazonaws.${region}.ssm | Interface | Depends (recommended) | Yes (recommended) | AWS Systems Manager API (managed instance) for Session Manager / patching | Data plane, Control plane | Only needed if customer wants SSM-based access; alternative: customer bastion/SSH via internal tooling | Optional
SSM Messages | com.amazonaws.${region}.ssmmessages | Interface | Depends | Yes (recommended) | Session Manager data channel | Data plane, Control plane | Must include ssm + ec2messages + ssmmessages together for SSM sessions | Optional
EC2 Messages | com.amazonaws.${region}.ec2messages | Interface | Depends | Yes (recommended) | Required for SSM agent comms | Data plane, Control plane | Same bundle as above | Optional

5) Encryption / secrets
KMS | com.amazonaws.${region}.kms | Interface | Depends | Yes (recommended) | Use customer-managed KMS keys (EBS encryption, secrets envelope, log bucket SSE-KMS) | Control plane, Data plane, Observability | If customer enforces CMKs for EBS/S3/Logs, treat as “effectively required”; include in locked-down profile | Optional (recommended in regulated profile)
Secrets Manager | com.amazonaws.${region}.secretsmanager | Interface | Optional/Depends | Yes (recommended) | Retrieve secrets at runtime (if customer integrates) | Control plane | Redwood Private can be deployed without Secrets Manager if using K8s secrets or customer vault; document choices | Optional
SSO / OIDC | (varies; often no endpoint) | N/A | Optional | N/A | If customer uses AWS SSO/OIDC flows, usually handled outside VPC | N/A | Do not assume VPC endpoints will satisfy SSO auth | N/A

6) Compute/control-plane adjacent (only if customer architecture uses these AWS services)
EKS | com.amazonaws.${region}.eks | Interface | Depends | Yes (recommended) | If Redwood Private uses EKS-managed control plane API in customer account | Installer, Control plane | Only needed if installation target is EKS; if using self-managed K8s, not required | Optional (profile-driven)
EC2 | com.amazonaws.${region}.ec2 | Interface | Depends | Yes (recommended) | If installer/control plane calls EC2 API from inside VPC (e.g., discovery/validation) | Installer (rare) | Prefer running API-calling steps from admin environment; keep out of default to avoid over-broad policies | Optional
ELB | com.amazonaws.${region}.elasticloadbalancing | Interface | Depends | Yes (recommended) | If provisioning/controlling ALB/NLB from inside VPC runtime | Installer (rare) | Generally IaC does this; runtime should not need it | Optional
Auto Scaling | com.amazonaws.${region}.autoscaling | Interface | Optional | Yes (recommended) | If nodes managed by ASG and scaling controlled from inside VPC | Control plane | Keep out of default; usually IaC/ops tooling handles | Optional

7) DNS / routing support (note: not classic “endpoints” but relevant to private-only)
Route53 Resolver (inbound/outbound endpoints) | (Route53 Resolver endpoints) | N/A | Depends | N/A | Required when customer needs hybrid DNS (on-prem) or custom resolution for Private DNS to work | Installer preflight, Control plane | Not created by our endpoint module; but docs must highlight prerequisites for “private-only endpoints” | Not in `vpc-endpoints`; documented prerequisite

================================================================================
Recommended endpoint bundles (for module presets)
================================================================================
Preset A — “Standard (NAT allowed)”
- Required: none strictly (NAT handles)
- Recommended anyway for reliability/cost: ECR API, ECR DKR, S3 gateway, CloudWatch Logs

Preset B — “Private-only / no public egress (alpha supported)”
- Required: ECR API, ECR DKR, S3 gateway, STS
- Recommended: CloudWatch Logs (or alternate internal log sink), KMS (if CMK enforced)
- Optional: SSM bundle (ssm, ssmmessages, ec2messages)

Preset C — “Regulated / audit-heavy” (alpha: supported with customer alignment)
- Required: same as Preset B
- Strongly recommended: KMS + CloudWatch Logs (or S3 log sink w/ SSE-KMS)
- Consider: Secrets Manager if customer mandates centralized secrets

================================================================================
Known failure modes observed in alpha development / pilot prep (captured for docs + preflight)
================================================================================
- Missing S3 gateway endpoint (or route table not associated with node subnets) → ECR pulls fail even if ECR endpoints exist.
- Missing STS endpoint in private-only networks → auth failures / token refresh failures; can present as “random” image pull issues.
- Private DNS disabled on interface endpoints without compensating DNS rules → installer can’t resolve standard AWS service hostnames.
- Endpoint association eventual consistency (timing) during terraform apply → transient failures; mitigate with explicit depends_on + retry (tracked in redwood-terraform PR-254).

TODO / open questions (track in ENG-4823 / ADR-0128 follow-ups)
- Do we want to include `monitoring` endpoint in “standard” by default, or keep strictly optional to reduce endpoint sprawl?
- Confirm whether installer ever calls AWS APIs from inside the VPC runtime in our reference architecture (prefer: no).
- Document explicit unsupported: “private-only” deployments without functional DNS (no Private DNS and no Route53 Resolver strategy).

Change log
- 2025-02-20: Marked STS as required for private-only; added SSM bundle notes; clarified S3 gateway route table association pitfall.
- 2025-02-05: Initial matrix drafted for alpha module implementation + installer preflight checks.
